name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
description: Provides support for eligible micro food processing enterprises, including credit-linked capital subsidy for individual micro food processing units.
target_segment: Micro food processing enterprises
eligibility_rules: Applicant should be involved in an eligible micro food processing activity.
Individual micro food processing units may receive credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of eligible project cost, subject to a maximum of Rs.10 lakh per unit.
Beneficiary contribution should be at least 10% of the project cost.
support_type: Credit-linked capital subsidy

name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
description: A credit-linked subsidy programme supporting eligible new micro-enterprises in manufacturing and service/trading activities.
target_segment: New micro-enterprises
eligibility_rules: The applicant must satisfy the eligibility conditions specified in the current PMEGP guidelines.
Maximum project cost for manufacturing units is Rs.50 lakh.
Maximum project cost for service/trading units is Rs.20 lakh.
Bank financing and beneficiary contribution are subject to the applicable PMEGP guidelines.
support_type: Credit-linked margin money subsidy
documents: Educational or training documents where applicable

name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
description: Provides collateral-free institutional credit to eligible micro enterprises for income-generating activities.
target_segment: Micro enterprises
eligibility_rules: Loans are intended for eligible non-agricultural income-generating micro enterprise activities, including specified allied agricultural activities.
Shishu loans are up to Rs.50,000.
Kishore loans are above Rs.50,000 and up to Rs.5 lakh.
Tarun loans are above Rs.5 lakh and up to Rs.10 lakh.
Tarun Plus loans are above Rs.10 lakh and up to Rs.20 lakh for entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid a previous Tarun-category loan.
support_type: Collateral-free business loan

name: PM Vishwakarma
description: Support for traditional artisans and craftspeople: skill training with a daily stipend, a toolkit incentive, and collateral-free credit at a concessional rate of interest.
target_segment: Traditional artisans and craftspeople working with hand tools
eligibility_rules: The applicant must work in a traditional trade using hand tools.
The applicant must work in one of the 18 trades covered by the scheme, such as tailoring, pottery, blacksmithy, carpentry, hair cutting, goldsmithy, basket weaving or cobbling.
A toolkit incentive of Rs.15,000 is available after basic skill training.
Collateral-free credit of up to Rs.1 lakh in the first tranche and up to Rs.2 lakh in the second, at 5% interest.
The applicant must be at least 18 years old.
support_type: Toolkit incentive, training stipend and concessional credit
documents: Verification letter from the Gram Panchayat or urban local body

name: Stand-Up India
description: Bank loans between Rs.10 lakh and Rs.1 crore for a first enterprise set up by a woman entrepreneur, or by an entrepreneur from a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe community.
target_segment: First-time women, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs
eligibility_rules: The enterprise must be majority owned and controlled by a woman, or by a person from a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe community.
The loan size ranges from Rs.10 lakh to Rs.1 crore.
The unit must be new, not an existing or transferred unit.
Activities allied to agriculture, such as dairy, poultry and food processing, are covered; crop cultivation on its own is not.
support_type: Bank loan for a first-time enterprise

name: National Livestock Mission - Entrepreneurship Development
description: Capital subsidy that does not have to be repaid, of up to half the project cost, for setting up poultry, sheep and goat, piggery, or feed and fodder units.
target_segment: Poultry, small ruminant, piggery and fodder entrepreneurs
eligibility_rules: Covers poultry, sheep and goat rearing, piggery, and feed and fodder units.
Up to 50% of the project cost is given as a subsidy that is not repaid, subject to a ceiling of Rs.50 lakh.
Relevant training or experience in the activity, and land for the unit, are required.
Final sanction rests with the financing bank.
support_type: Capital subsidy of up to half the project cost
documents: Ownership or rent agreement for the work premises
Details of livestock held or planned

name: Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)
description: A bank loan on which the government pays part of the interest, for setting up milk chilling and milk product units, meat processing units, and animal feed plants.
target_segment: Dairy, meat and animal feed processing units
eligibility_rules: Covers milk chilling and dairy product units, meat processing units, and animal feed plants.
An interest subvention of 3% is available for up to eight years.
The applicant must contribute at least 10% of the project cost.
support_type: Bank loan with 3% of the interest paid by government
documents: Ownership or rent agreement for the work premises
Udyam registration number, where already held

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
description: A loan of up to Rs.2 crore on which the government pays 3% of the interest, for storage, cold rooms, grading and packing, and small units that process farm produce.
target_segment: Post-harvest and primary processing projects
eligibility_rules: Covers post-harvest work such as storage, cold rooms, grading and packing houses, and primary processing units.
Interest subvention of 3% applies on a loan of up to Rs.2 crore, for up to seven years.
Farmers, self-help groups, farmer producer organisations and micro enterprises may apply.
support_type: Loan with 3% of the interest paid by government
documents: Quotations for machinery, tools or equipment

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
description: A card from your bank for short-term borrowing at a concessional rate of interest, repayable after harvest. Animal husbandry and fisheries are also covered.
target_segment: Farmers, tenant farmers and share-croppers
eligibility_rules: Available to land-owning farmers, tenant farmers, share-croppers and joint liability groups.
Interest is 7% on credit up to Rs.3 lakh, reduced to 4% on timely repayment.
Animal husbandry and fisheries are covered up to Rs.2 lakh.
support_type: Concessional short-term credit from your bank

name: Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Vikas Abhiyan (MYUVA), Uttar Pradesh
description: For young people in Uttar Pradesh starting their own enterprise: a project of up to Rs.5 lakh financed on an interest-free basis, arranged through the District Industries Centre.
target_segment: Young first-generation entrepreneurs in Uttar Pradesh
eligibility_rules: The applicant must generally be between 21 and 40 years of age.
The applicant must have passed at least class 8, or hold a recognised skill training certificate.
Project cost of up to Rs.5 lakh is financed, with no interest payable by the beneficiary for the stated period.
The applicant must be a resident of the state.
support_type: Interest-free loan of up to Rs.5 lakh
documents: Domicile or residence certificate for the state
Educational or training documents where applicable

name: Vishwakarma Shram Samman Yojana, Uttar Pradesh
description: Six days of free skill training and a free toolkit for traditional workers in Uttar Pradesh - tailors, potters, blacksmiths, carpenters, barbers, cobblers and others.
target_segment: Traditional artisans in Uttar Pradesh
eligibility_rules: The applicant must work in a traditional trade using hand tools.
Covers traditional trades such as tailoring, pottery, blacksmithy, carpentry, hair cutting and shoe making.
The applicant must be at least 18 years old.
The applicant must be a resident of the state.
No fee is charged for this assistance.
support_type: Free skill training and a free toolkit
documents: Domicile or residence certificate for the state

name: Chief Minister's Employment Generation Programme (CMEGP), Maharashtra
description: For new small units in Maharashtra: a bank loan with 15% to 35% of the project cost provided as a subsidy that is not repaid.
target_segment: New micro and small units in Maharashtra
eligibility_rules: The applicant must generally be between 18 and 45 years of age.
Project cost may go up to Rs.50 lakh for manufacturing and Rs.10 lakh for service activities.
A subsidy of 15% to 35% of project cost applies, depending on the applicant category and the location of the unit.
The unit must be new, not an existing or transferred unit.
support_type: Bank loan with part of the project cost as subsidy
documents: Domicile or residence certificate for the state
Educational or training documents where applicable

name: New Entrepreneur cum Enterprise Development Scheme (NEEDS), Tamil Nadu
description: For educated young people in Tamil Nadu setting up a unit: business training, a bank loan, and 25% of the project cost as a subsidy that is not repaid.
target_segment: Educated first-generation entrepreneurs in Tamil Nadu
eligibility_rules: The applicant must be at least 21 years old and hold a degree, diploma or ITI qualification.
A capital subsidy of 25% of the project cost applies, on project cost of up to Rs.75 lakh.
Training forms part of the scheme.
The applicant must be a resident of the state.
support_type: Training, bank loan and a 25% subsidy
documents: Domicile or residence certificate for the state
Educational or training documents where applicable

name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme (ESS), Kerala
description: Kerala pays back part of what you spend on land, building, machinery and electric fitting for a small manufacturing unit - from 15% up to 45% for some groups of people.
target_segment: Micro and small manufacturing units in Kerala
eligibility_rules: Open to micro and small manufacturing units registered in Kerala.
Assistance ranges from 15% to 45% of eligible investment, with the higher rates for women, young entrepreneurs, and applicants from Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities.
Part of the assistance may be claimed before commencement and the balance after the unit starts production.
Udyam registration is required.
support_type: Part of your set-up spending paid back
documents: Udyam registration number, where already held
Ownership or rent agreement for the work premises
Quotations for machinery, tools or equipment

name: Bhabishyat Credit Card, West Bengal
description: For young people in West Bengal starting their own work: a project of up to Rs.5 lakh, guaranteed by the state, with 10% of the cost given as a subsidy.
target_segment: Young entrepreneurs in West Bengal
eligibility_rules: The applicant must generally be between 18 and 45 years of age.
Project cost of up to Rs.5 lakh is covered, and the state provides the credit guarantee.
A subsidy of 10% of the project cost is provided and is not repaid.
The applicant must be a resident of the state.
support_type: State-guaranteed loan with a 10% subsidy
documents: Domicile or residence certificate for the state

name: Udyogini, Karnataka
description: For women in Karnataka running or starting a small business: a loan of up to Rs.3 lakh, with part of it given as a subsidy for women from certain groups.
target_segment: Women entrepreneurs in Karnataka
eligibility_rules: Only women applicants are eligible.
Loans of up to Rs.3 lakh are available for the listed categories of business.
A subsidy of 30% of the loan, up to Rs.90,000, applies for applicants from Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and other specified categories.
A family income ceiling applies, except for widows and women with a disability.
The applicant must be a resident of the state.
support_type: Loan for women with part given as subsidy

name: UNNATI 2024 - Uttar Poorva Transformative Industrialization Scheme
description: For new and growing units in the eight North Eastern states: money towards the cost of your building, plant and machinery, along with other production-linked support.
target_segment: New and expanding units in the eight North Eastern states
eligibility_rules: The unit must be located in one of the eight North Eastern states.
Capital investment incentive is provided towards plant, machinery and building, at a higher rate in the more remote districts.
Registration on the scheme portal is required before commencing the investment.
Udyam registration is required.
support_type: Money towards your building, plant and machinery
documents: Udyam registration number, where already held
Ownership or rent agreement for the work premises
Quotations for machinery, tools or equipment

name: Vibrant Villages Programme
description: For villages in the notified border blocks of the northern and north-eastern hills: support to build local earning work such as home-stays, dairy and animal keeping, and craft.
target_segment: Villages in notified border blocks of the northern and north-eastern hills
eligibility_rules: Only villages in the border blocks notified under the programme are covered.
Support is directed at home-stays and rural tourism, dairy and animal husbandry, craft, and small local enterprise.
Rates and conditions vary by location, so confirm them at the local office.
support_type: Support to build local earning work
documents: Verification letter from the Gram Panchayat or urban local body

name: District Industries Centre (DIC)
description: The government office in your own district that registers small enterprises, sends your subsidy and loan applications on to the state and central schemes, and tells you which ones you qualify for.
target_segment: Micro and small enterprises in the district
eligibility_rules: Anyone carrying on or planning work in the area may approach the office.
The office handles Udyam registration, forwards applications under state and central schemes, and arranges entrepreneurship training.
No fee is charged for this assistance.
support_type: Free help with registration and scheme applications
documents: Udyam registration number, where already held

name: Rural Self Employment Training Institute (RSETI)
description: A free training institute in your district, run with the banks. You stay there for one to six weeks, learn a trade, and the institute then helps you apply for a loan and keeps following up.
target_segment: Rural youth in the district
eligibility_rules: The applicant must generally be between 18 and 45 years of age.
The applicant must be from a rural area of the district.
Training, boarding and lodging are provided at no cost to the trainee.
After training the institute assists with the loan application and follows up for about two years.
support_type: Free training with food and stay, and loan help after
documents: Educational or training documents where applicable

name: Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK)
description: The farm science centre in your district. It gives free advice and short courses on dairy, poultry, beekeeping, mushroom growing and food making, and it tests your soil.
target_segment: Farmers and rural workers in the district
eligibility_rules: Farmers, farm labourers and farm groups of the area are eligible.
Short courses are run on animal husbandry, beekeeping, mushroom cultivation, food processing and seed production.
No fee is charged for this assistance.
support_type: Free training, advice and soil testing

name: One District One Product (ODOP), Uttar Pradesh
description: Every district in Uttar Pradesh has one chosen craft or product. If your work is your district's product, you can get a toolkit, training, help selling at fairs, and margin money on a loan.
target_segment: Artisans and units working on their district's notified product
eligibility_rules: Your activity must be the product notified for your own district - ask your District Industries Centre which one it is.
Trained artisans receive a toolkit and may take part in state and national fairs.
A loan with margin money assistance is available under the ODOP financing component.
The applicant must be a resident of the state.
support_type: Toolkit, training, help selling, and margin money
documents: Domicile or residence certificate for the state

name: Tehsil or Taluka office - certificates for scheme applications
description: Almost every scheme asks for an income, caste or residence certificate, and your tehsil or taluka office is what issues them. Get them before you apply anywhere else, or the application will be held up.
target_segment: Anyone applying to a government scheme
eligibility_rules: The office issues income, caste, residence and land-related certificates.
A certificate is usually issued within a few working days once the papers are complete.
Many states also accept these applications online or through a Common Service Centre.
support_type: The certificates other schemes ask you for

name: Sub-Divisional Agriculture Office
description: The agriculture office for your tehsil or sub-division. It sanctions the government share on seeds, hand tools, small machines and drip or sprinkler watering, and its staff come out to villages.
target_segment: Farmers in the sub-division
eligibility_rules: Farmers, farm labourers and farm groups of the area are eligible.
A share of the cost of seeds, hand tools, small farm machinery and micro-irrigation is met by the government.
Rates and conditions vary by location, so confirm them at the local office.
support_type: Government share on farm tools and inputs
documents: Quotations for machinery, tools or equipment

name: Block Development Office - rural livelihoods team
description: Your block office runs the rural livelihoods mission. Its team helps form self-help groups, gives a group its own money to lend to its members, and trains members to start small work.
target_segment: Rural families and self-help group members in the block
eligibility_rules: Rural households are covered, in particular women joining a self-help group.
A well-functioning group receives a revolving fund and a community investment fund to on-lend to its members.
The Lakhpati Didi effort supports women members in building annual earnings of a lakh or more.
Membership of a self-help group is required.
support_type: Group funds and training through your block

name: Block Level Bankers' Committee (BLBC)
description: Every block has a standing meeting of all its bank branches together with block officers. If a branch refuses or sits on your scheme loan without a clear reason, your case can be raised here.
target_segment: Applicants whose scheme loan is stuck or refused
eligibility_rules: Anyone carrying on or planning work in the area may approach the office.
Ask your block office or bank branch for the date of the next meeting and how to place your case before it.
The committee meets once a quarter and reviews the block credit plan and pending applications.
support_type: A place to take a refused or delayed scheme loan

name: ATMA - block farm technology team
description: The block farm team under ATMA runs field demonstrations and farmer field schools, arranges study visits to other districts, and pays a small allowance while you train.
target_segment: Farmers and farm groups in the block
eligibility_rules: Farmers, farm labourers and farm groups of the area are eligible.
Field demonstrations, farmer field schools, and sponsored study visits within and outside the district are provided.
Each village has a designated farmer friend who can be approached first.
support_type: Free farm training and study visits

name: Gram Panchayat - trade permission and village plan
description: Your Gram Panchayat issues the no-objection letter and trade permission a village shop or small unit needs, and its yearly village plan can pay for a shed, water or an approach road to your work place.
target_segment: Work carried on within the Gram Panchayat area
eligibility_rules: Anyone carrying on or planning work in the area may approach the office.
The Panchayat issues a no-objection letter and trade permission, and verifies your papers for other schemes.
Ask for your requirement to be included in the yearly Gram Panchayat Development Plan at the Gram Sabha meeting.
support_type: Trade permission and village plan works
documents: Ownership or rent agreement for the work premises

name: Common Service Centre (CSC) - Digital Seva Kendra
description: The village computer centre. The operator fills online scheme forms for you, scans your papers, and handles Aadhaar, bank and certificate work for a small fixed charge.
target_segment: Anyone in the village or ward
eligibility_rules: Anyone carrying on or planning work in the area may approach the office.
The operator can register you under PM Vishwakarma, MUDRA and other schemes, and print the acknowledgement.
A small fixed service charge applies for each service.
An Aadhaar card and a bank account in the applicant's own name are required.
support_type: Help to fill online scheme forms
documents: Working mobile number linked to Aadhaar

name: PM SVANidhi - through your urban local body
description: For street vendors in a town or city. The vending certificate or survey letter from your local body gets you a working capital loan of Rs.10,000, then Rs.20,000, then Rs.50,000, with money back for repaying on time.
target_segment: Street vendors in a town or city area
eligibility_rules: The activity must be in a town or city area covered by an urban local body.
The vendor must have been covered by the local body vending survey, or hold a certificate of vending or a letter of recommendation.
The first loan is Rs.10,000; on timely repayment the next is Rs.20,000, and then Rs.50,000.
Digital transactions earn cash back, and timely repayment earns a 7% interest subsidy.
No collateral has to be pledged.
support_type: Working capital loan for street vendors
documents: Certificate of vending or the local body survey letter
